text: 📸 Honestidad y resultados — Hermosillo, Sonora, 26 de septiembre de 2026

🇲🇽🌎 "To this day the powers see Mexico as an opportunity, because of its natural resources. But here there are always the people of Mexico, with their memory, with their history, defending the homeland." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Hermosillo, Sonora In Hermosillo she ran through what came after independence: Spain's 1829 attempt to invade again, the French Pastry War, the US invasion that took more than half the territory, the French intervention defeated under Benito Juárez, the 1913 coup against Madero led by US Ambassador Henry Lane Wilson, and the US attempt to invade again in 1914.
banner: 1913 COUP LED BY THE US AMBASSADOR

text: 🇲🇽✊ "It was all a hoax. They did not want justice for the people." "The minimum wage went up 154% in real terms, and there is no inflation, no devaluation of the peso, and we are at a record of foreign direct investment." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Hermosillo, Sonora The minimum wage was 2,800 pesos a month in 2018; today it is more than 9,500. In the neoliberal era they warned that raising it would bring inflation, devaluation and no investment. "The poor are poor because they don't work. False. It was an economic model that generated poverty."
banner: MINIMUM WAGE: UP 154% IN REAL TERMS

text: 🇲🇽📚 "The word is equality, not inequality." "In the classroom a false division was created between the supposedly good student and the bad student. Instead of making them more interested in studying, they felt less, they felt discriminated against." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Hermosillo, Sonora As head of government of Mexico City she replaced a scholarship for students with 9–10 averages with a universal one, and grades went up for everyone. In Sonora, together with Governor Alfonso Durazo, every public-school student now has a scholarship, from primary school to university: 155,255 primary, 113,736 secondary, 99,116 high school and 97,689 university students.

🇲🇽✊ "Justice for Indigenous peoples. The Yaqui people alone have had more than 45,000 hectares returned." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Hermosillo, Sonora In Sonora, she said, justice has meant every kind of justice: labor justice for the Cananea miners, whose historic conflict was resolved; environmental justice, with one of the companies that most polluted the Sonora River paying 100 million pesos for the river's cleanup and hospitals; and land for the Yaqui, who suffered the worst of the Porfirio Díaz repression. The aqueduct López Obrador began for the Yaqui people is now finished.
banner: SONORA: 45,000 HECTARES BACK TO THE YAQUI

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "No president can have two flags or two peoples. Only the flag of Mexico and the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Hermosillo, Sonora Her constitutional reform barring anyone with dual nationality from being president was approved by the Chamber of Deputies and goes to the Senate this week, then to the state congresses. "People can have double, triple nationality, but if you want to be president of Mexico or governor of any Mexican state, you can only be Mexican." Many legislators did not vote for it.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Economy jumps 0.8% in July, beating forecasts</u>

INEGI's IGAE grew 0.8% month-on-month in July — eight times the 0.1% its own timely indicator had projected — and 3.3% year-on-year, El Economista reports.

Services rose 1.2% in the month, their biggest jump in over two years, and 4.0% annually, while industry grew 2.4%. Analysts at Valmex expect services and construction to keep driving growth, "backed by resilient domestic demand."

🇲🇽🇷🇺 <u>Mexico and Russia agree to deepen ties at the UN</u>

On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco sat down with Sergey Lavrov on Saturday. The two agreed to keep bilateral political dialogue open and to expand trade, economic, cultural and humanitarian cooperation.

They highlighted joint work at the UN, the G20 and APEC, and reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of international law. Mexico and Russia have kept diplomatic relations since 1890.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mazatlán: 8 cartel suspects arrested, 14 explosives seized</u>

Seven federal operations in Mazatlán, Sinaloa netted eight suspected members of Sinaloa Cartel cells, 19 firearms, more than 2,000 cartridges, 14 homemade explosive devices and 415 fentanyl pills.

Among those detained: Erik Samuel Barraza Sánchez, "Fantasma," alleged head of a Los Mayos cell, and José Luis Ibarra Gutiérrez, "El Prieto," tied to Los Chapitos. In El Quelite, SSPC agents were shot at, repelled the attack and arrested six. Both warring factions hit in the same sweep.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The architects of Fobaproa still out-earn the President</u>

Contralínea lays out the Banxico pension list: Miguel Mancera collects 412,472 pesos a month, Francisco Gil Díaz 359,078, Francisco Rueda 349,677, Guillermo Ortiz 329,920, Agustín Carstens 157,429 and Ernesto Zedillo 149,203 — every one above Sheinbaum's constitutional salary of 134,290.

Around 50 former Banxico officials draw 150,000 to 400,000 pesos monthly, shielded by the central bank's autonomy and court injunctions. The men behind bank privatization and the Fobaproa bailout. Sheinbaum has put the pensions under review: "It may be legal, but not very fair."
